title: Generating Documents
text: These questions check that you can fill in a document template, build a document, work with Drive IDs, and organize a script so its calculations can be tested.

tasks.text: A document's address is https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcD2eFg/edit. What is its ID?
A certificate script fills in a copy of the template, then makes a PDF, but the PDF still shows {{First Name}}. What was most likely left out?
Why keep TEMPLATE_ID as a constant at the top of the file?
choices: Apps Script requires IDs to be at the top.
It's a setting every function can use, and there's one place to change it.

tasks.text: In the certificate script, why is it important that setTrashed(true) is called on copyFile and not templateFile? How would you check this before running the script on every member?
tasks.answer: Trashing the template would destroy the original, and every later certificate would fail. Read the line carefully, and test on one certificate (e.g. a test function) and check that the template is still in Drive afterward.

tasks.text: The newsletter script has getCropTotals(harvestData), which returns an object, and addHarvestTable(body, cropTotals), which changes a document. Which can you test on this book's pages, and why is it useful to write scripts this way?
tasks.answer: getCropTotals: it only calculates from an array and creates nothing. Keeping calculations separate from actions lets you test the bug-prone part anywhere, quickly and safely, and keeps the part that creates files small.

tasks.text: Write a function fillTemplate(text, member) that returns text with {{First Name}} and {{Hours}} replaced by member.firstName and member.hours, using the string method replace (which replaces the first match). Then write testFillTemplate, which logs fillTemplate("Thank you, {{First Name}}, for {{Hours}} hours!", { firstName: "Hana", hours: 18.5 }). (Expected: Thank you, Hana, for 18.5 hours!)

Start a new chat with your updated learner profile and the garden context. Ask for a script that creates one Google Doc listing every bed, with its name, size and sun, as a table, plus a heading. (1) Paste the reply. (2) Did it follow the updated dry-run rule for creating a file? How? (3) Which part could you test on this book's pages? (4) Run it in Apps Script and check the table against the Beds sheet.
tasks.answer: Full credit: identifies how the rule was followed (log, one-item test, or asking first); identifies a pure data function that could be tested on the page (or notes there isn't one and suggests one); table checked against the sheet. Replies vary, so grade the reasoning.
